name: esap
description: Emil's Super App Planner, as dsh runs it. A worked example, not a default: copy it to dsh.workspace.json in your own project and change every emils-planner-* name, because those are esap's crates and nothing here is generic.

setup.description: Without this the routing tests fail by the dozen for a missing DLL, and a run spends its whole budget reading failures that are not its fault.
ui_spec measures the real app, so it has to exist before the first spec runs. This is why ui_spec's own timeout is an hour: on a cold worktree the build is the slow part, and it happens here, once.

run_test.description: Run one Rust integration test file: the crate, and the file's name under that crate's tests/ without .rs. Run the one your task touches, not the whole suite. These four crates are the ones that have a tests/ directory; use run_unit_tests for the others.

test.description: the test file's name, as comments for crates/emils-planner-core/tests/comments.rs

run_unit_tests.description: Run the unit tests inside one crate's src/ (the #[cfg(test)] modules), for a crate your task changed.

registry.description: Run the core's registry tests: every command appears in the every_command sample once, is described, and parses. Run it whenever you add or change a core command.

ui_spec.description: Run one Playwright UI spec against the real app, by the spec file's name under ui/ without .spec.ts. It takes the project's machine lock, so it waits if another measurement is running. Slow, and only meaningful once your code compiles: run it once, not after every edit.

name.description: the spec's name, as grouped for ui/grouped.spec.ts

vitest.description: Run one vitest file under src/.

file.description: a path under src/, as src/commit.test.ts
